真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 86 页

原第1–4段连续裁切；词表A–J保留原题所有选项，含OCR漏掉的I已按原选项和答案页恢复。NG21已核对完整文章。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1The crowded and bustling streets of Delhi teem with life. Stop to listen and, above the din of rickshaws and buses, you'll hear a multitude of languages, as more than 20 million people go about their daily lives. Many were born and raised here, and many millions more have recently made India's capital their home, having moved from surrounding neighbourhoods, cities and states or across the country, often in the hope of gaining better jobs and a better life. Some arrive speaking fluent Hindi, the dominant language in Delhi (and the official language of government), but many arrive speaking any number of India's 22 officially recognised languages, let alone the hundreds of regional languages in a country of more than 1.3 billion people.

原文片段 · 2A team of researchers led by Professor Ianthi Tsimpli of Cambridge University is currently working on a project collecting data on 1,000 primary-age children in Delhi and the cities of Hyderabad and Bihar. The overriding aim of the four-year project, called 'Multilingualism and Multiliteracy', is to find out why in a country where multilingualism is so common (more than 255 million people in India speak at least two languages, and nearly 90 million speak three or more languages), the many benefits of speaking more than one language, observed in schools in Europe for instance, do not apply to many of India's schoolchildren.

原文片段 · 3'Each year across India, 600,000 children are tested, and year after year over 50% of children in Standard 5 [ten-year-olds] cannot read a Standard 2 [seven-year-olds] task fluently, and just under 50% of them cannot solve a Standard 2 subtraction task,' says Tsimpli. She explains that low educational achievement can lead to many of these students dropping out of school - a problem disproportionately affecting female students.

原文片段 · 4Tsimpli and her colleagues are investigating whether these low learning outcomes could be caused by an Indian school system where the language that children are taught in often differs from the language used at home. The research project, which focuses on 8 to 11-year old schoolchildren in rural and urban areas, collects data on whether the schoolchildren live in slum* or non-slum areas. Many of the children have moved from remote, rural areas to urban areas. They are so poor they have to live in slums and, as a result of migration, they may speak languages that are different from the regional language.

题目与作答

按原题号作答。保留考试原文与题目难度；以下是连续原段裁切，未改写原文。

共用选项 · 原题 14、15、16、17、18、19

  • A. basic outlook
  • B. employment opportunities
  • C. wealthy visitors
  • D. distant country
  • E. primary objective
  • F. similar advantages
  • G. thriving economy
  • H. nearby district
  • I. dense population
  • J. new immigrants

14. The city of Delhi has a ______ and as you walk through its streets you hear people speaking a variety of languages.

Complete the summary using the list of words below. Write the correct letter for each answer.

15. Some of them have spent their entire life in Delhi, while others are ______.

Complete the summary using the list of words below. Write the correct letter for each answer.

16. Whether they have come from a ______ or have travelled from the other side of India,

Complete the summary using the list of words below. Write the correct letter for each answer.

17. they have all come in search of things such as improved ______.

Complete the summary using the list of words below. Write the correct letter for each answer.

18. The ______ of the research is to discover why multilingual Indian schoolchildren do not experience

Complete the summary using the list of words below. Write the correct letter for each answer.

19. ______ to those that multilingual schoolchildren in Europe experience.

Complete the summary using the list of words below. Write the correct letter for each answer.

20. Ten-year-old Indian schoolchildren tend to perform better in literacy tests than in numeracy tests.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

21. Tsimpli had problems convincing some female students to take part in the study.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

22. Tsimpli and her team wanted to know if there is a connection between poor academic performance and being taught in an unfamiliar language.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

对照答案，回到证据

第 14 题 · I

crowded与2000多万人对应dense population；不是只因bustling就选thriving economy。

The crowded and bustling streets of Delhi teem with life ... more than 20 million people

第 15 题 · J

recently迁入与new immigrants对应；不等于wealthy visitors短期游客。

many millions more have recently made India’s capital their home, having moved from ...

第 16 题 · H

surrounding neighbourhoods对应nearby district，与other side形成近/远对照；原文不是移自国外。

having moved from surrounding neighbourhoods, cities and states or across the country

第 17 题 · B

better jobs对应employment opportunities；不要凭“更好生活”添富游客身份。

often in the hope of gaining better jobs and a better life

第 18 题 · E

overriding aim同义于primary objective，句法也需要单数研究目标。

The overriding aim of the four-year project ... is to find out why

第 19 题 · F

benefits对应advantages；研究问为何并未获得相似收益。

the many benefits ... observed in schools in Europe ... do not apply to many of India’s schoolchildren

第 20 题 · NO

识字不达标超过50%，计算不达标略低于50%，方向与better in literacy相反；比较的是不能完成的比例。

over 50% ... cannot read ... and just under 50% ... cannot solve ... subtraction

第 21 题 · NOT GIVEN

女生受退学影响更多不是难以说服参加研究；全文没有recruitment问题。

low educational achievement ... dropping out of school ... disproportionately affecting female students

第 22 题 · YES

研究的问题正是低学习表现与教学/家庭语言不一致是否有关。

investigating whether these low learning outcomes could be caused by ... language ... taught in often differs from ... used at home

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

德里的语言多样性来自长期居住与人口迁移。研究关注一个表面矛盾：社会中多语现象普遍，一些学生却没有呈现其他教育环境里观察到的益处。文章把调查问题落到家庭语言、学校授课语言、贫困与学习环境之间的关系，而未先判定多语本身有害。

原文片段 · 1

The crowded and bustling streets of Delhi teem with life. Stop to listen and, above the din of rickshaws and buses, you'll hear a multitude of languages, as more than 20 million people go about their daily lives. Many were born and raised here, and many millions more have recently made India's capital their home, having moved from surrounding neighbourhoods, cities and states or across the country, often in the hope of gaining better jobs and a better life. Some arrive speaking fluent Hindi, the dominant language in Delhi (and the official language of government), but many arrive speaking any number of India's 22 officially recognised languages, let alone the hundreds of regional languages in a country of more than 1.3 billion people.

繁忙街道的声音引出多语言共存，迁入者常怀着更好工作和生活的希望来到首都。有人熟练使用占主导地位的印地语，也有人主要使用其他官方或地区语言。let alone 强调官方语言数量之外还有更多地区语言；统计值与人口描述沿用原文时点。

原文片段 · 2

A team of researchers led by Professor Ianthi Tsimpli of Cambridge University is currently working on a project collecting data on 1,000 primary-age children in Delhi and the cities of Hyderabad and Bihar. The overriding aim of the four-year project, called 'Multilingualism and Multiliteracy', is to find out why in a country where multilingualism is so common (more than 255 million people in India speak at least two languages, and nearly 90 million speak three or more languages), the many benefits of speaking more than one language, observed in schools in Europe for instance, do not apply to many of India's schoolchildren.

研究团队对千名小学年龄儿童收集资料，目标不是证明会多种语言一定有益或有害，而是理解为何在某些欧洲学校观察到的益处没有出现在许多印度学生身上。observed in schools in Europe 限定比较经验的来源，不能把它扩大为所有欧洲儿童的普遍结论。

原文片段 · 3

'Each year across India, 600,000 children are tested, and year after year over 50% of children in Standard 5 [ten-year-olds] cannot read a Standard 2 [seven-year-olds] task fluently, and just under 50% of them cannot solve a Standard 2 subtraction task,' says Tsimpli. She explains that low educational achievement can lead to many of these students dropping out of school - a problem disproportionately affecting female students.

研究者引述重复出现的低学习表现：许多五年级儿童仍难以完成二年级阅读和减法任务。这里的比较体现学习进展不足，后果可能是辍学，且女生受到不成比例的影响。can lead to 是风险关系，不是说每个表现偏低的儿童都会离校。

原文片段 · 4

Tsimpli and her colleagues are investigating whether these low learning outcomes could be caused by an Indian school system where the language that children are taught in often differs from the language used at home. The research project, which focuses on 8 to 11-year old schoolchildren in rural and urban areas, collects data on whether the schoolchildren live in slum* or non-slum areas. Many of the children have moved from remote, rural areas to urban areas. They are so poor they have to live in slums and, as a result of migration, they may speak languages that are different from the regional language.

研究进一步检查学校授课语言与家庭语言不同是否可能影响学习，同时记录城乡、住区和迁移背景。家庭贫困限制居住选择，迁移又可能造成儿童原有语言与迁入地语言不同。whether 和 could be caused 表示研究中的问题，不能直接改成已经确定的唯一原因。

词语与搭配

in the hope of gaining better jobs and a better life

怀着获得更好工作与生活的希望

in the hope of 后接动名词，表达迁移者的动机，不表示愿望必然实现。

The overriding aim

最主要的目标

overriding 强调优先地位；原文用来概括项目需要回答的核心问题。

low educational achievement

较低的学习成就

在文中由具体阅读与计算表现说明，不能直接等同于儿童智力较低。

differs from the language used at home

与家庭使用的语言不同

differ from 比较两个明确对象，这里是学校教学语言和家庭语言。

句子精读

Tsimpli and her colleagues are investigating whether these low learning outcomes could be caused by an Indian school system where the language that children are taught in often differs from the language used at home.

Tsimpli 和同事正在调查，这些较低的学习成果是否可能与印度学校的一种情况有关：儿童接受教学的语言常常不同于家里使用的语言。

whether 从句是 investigating 的内容，could be caused 保留待验证的可能性。where 描述学校体系中的情况；that children are taught in 修饰 language，句末的 in 与该语言搭配，表示以某种语言授课。

They are so poor they have to live in slums and, as a result of migration, they may speak languages that are different from the regional language.

这些儿童的家庭十分贫困，以至于他们不得不住在贫民区；而且，由于迁移，他们使用的语言可能不同于当地的地区语言。

They 回指从偏远农村迁往城市的许多儿童。so poor 后省略了 that，引出居住条件的结果。and 后另加迁移造成的语言差异，may 保留个体差别；贫困与语言差异不是完全相同的一个原因。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

differs from the language used at home

与家庭语言不同

适合解释某些儿童理解课堂内容时面临的额外要求，避免把语言差异等同于能力不足。

用于写作：小学正式学习与游戏题关注课堂学习体验；可用来说明具体情境下游戏和实物活动怎样支持理解，不把游戏宣称为所有语言困难的解决方案。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
Multilingualism · 教学语言与出人意料的结果未作答观点判断 YNNG / 选择题 · 4 段 · 362 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 87 页

原第5–8段连续裁切；题面sixth/eighth paragraph分别对应本片段第2/4段。保留may、might、preliminary等不确定表达。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1Having already tested 1,000 children, the researchers will now embark on retesting them. They intend to look not only at test results, but also at variables such as the standard of schooling, the environment and the teaching practices themselves. It's possible that one of the causes of low performance is the lack of pupil-centred teaching methods; in many Indian primary schools the teacher dominates and there is little room for independent learning.

原文片段 · 2Although the findings are at a preliminary stage, Tsimpli and her team have found that the medium of instruction used in schools, especially English, may hold back those children who have little familiarity with, or exposure to, the language before starting school and outside of school life. According to Tsimpli, most of the evidence from this and other projects shows that English instruction for children from low socio-economic areas might not be the best way for them to learn, at least in the first three years of primary education.

原文片段 · 3'What we would recommend for everyone, not just low socio-economic status children, would be to start learning in the language they feel comfortable learning in ... English can still be used, but perhaps not as the medium of instruction in primary schools. It could, for example, be one of the subjects that are being taught alongside other subjects. We are not suggesting that English be withdrawn - that ship has sailed - but we perhaps have to think more about learner needs. There is perhaps too much uniformity in teaching and less tailoring to the children's language abilities and needs,' says Tsimpli.

原文片段 · 4While the preliminary results show there is no difference in general intelligence among boys and girls from slum areas versus those from urban poor backgrounds, an unanticipated finding has been that children from slum backgrounds do not seem to lag behind children from other urban poor backgrounds - and in some cases outperform them (e.g. in numeracy and literacy tasks). According to the researchers, this unexpected finding may be down to the life experiences of children growing up in slums. They are likely to mature faster and come into closer contact with the numeracy skills essential for day-to-day survival.

题目与作答

按原题号作答。保留考试原文与题目难度；以下是连续原段裁切，未改写原文。

23. The researchers have decided against investigating the impact teaching methodology may have on learning outcomes.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

24. What point does the writer make about primary schools in India in the sixth paragraph?

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. Exposure to English outside of school is of limited benefit.
  • B. Children learn English more easily when they are well motivated.
  • C. Poor children may be disadvantaged further by being instructed in English.
  • D. There is little consistency across schools with regard to instruction in English.

25. What is Tsimpli suggesting when she uses the phrase 'that ship has sailed'?

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. The findings of the report may be of little help to some Indian schoolchildren.
  • B. Instruction in English could be better adapted to the needs of schoolchildren.
  • C. Schools have had limited success in teaching English as a separate subject.
  • D. It is too late to remove English completely as a language of instruction in schools.

26. In the eighth paragraph, what do we learn has surprised researchers?

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. Boys and girls from low socio-economic groups have similar general intelligence levels.
  • B. The age at which children move into a slum does not affect their academic performance.
  • C. Slum children and children from other urban poor backgrounds have similar life experiences.
  • D. The literacy and numeracy skills of slum children are not lower than those of children from other urban poor backgrounds.

对照答案，回到证据

第 23 题 · NO

intend to investigate practices直接反驳decided against investigating methodology。

They intend to look not only at test results, but also ... the teaching practices themselves

第 24 题 · C

不熟悉教学用英语可能进一步拖住贫困儿童；不是说动机能使英语更容易学。

English, may hold back those children who have little familiarity with, or exposure to, the language

第 25 题 · D

紧贴前半句be withdrawn理解：完全撤回英语已不现实。B是后文改进方向，却不是该习语所指。

We are not suggesting that English be withdrawn - that ship has sailed

第 26 题 · D

unanticipated锁定意外发现：贫民窟儿童读写算并未落后，有时更好；general intelligence相同只是前面的背景。

an unanticipated finding ... children from slum backgrounds do not seem to lag behind ... and in some cases outperform them

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

研究开始把授课语言、教学方式与儿童生活经验一起考虑。作者呈现的是初步结果：陌生的授课语言可能阻碍早期学习，贴合儿童需求比统一要求更合适；贫困住区儿童某些表现较好也不能反过来证明贫困本身有益。

原文片段 · 1

Having already tested 1,000 children, the researchers will now embark on retesting them. They intend to look not only at test results, but also at variables such as the standard of schooling, the environment and the teaching practices themselves. It's possible that one of the causes of low performance is the lack of pupil-centred teaching methods; in many Indian primary schools the teacher dominates and there is little room for independent learning.

再次测试让研究者能继续观察儿童，而不只停留在一次结果。他们也看学校质量、环境和课堂做法；教师主导、缺少自主学习空间只是一个可能原因。It's possible 和 one of the causes 同时限制了因果判断。

原文片段 · 2

Although the findings are at a preliminary stage, Tsimpli and her team have found that the medium of instruction used in schools, especially English, may hold back those children who have little familiarity with, or exposure to, the language before starting school and outside of school life. According to Tsimpli, most of the evidence from this and other projects shows that English instruction for children from low socio-economic areas might not be the best way for them to learn, at least in the first three years of primary education.

研究初步发现，入学前及校外很少接触某种授课语言的儿童，可能受到语言本身的阻碍。关于英语不一定最适合的判断，特别限定在经济社会条件较弱儿童的小学前三年，不能读成所有年龄都不该学英语。

原文片段 · 3

'What we would recommend for everyone, not just low socio-economic status children, would be to start learning in the language they feel comfortable learning in ... English can still be used, but perhaps not as the medium of instruction in primary schools. It could, for example, be one of the subjects that are being taught alongside other subjects. We are not suggesting that English be withdrawn - that ship has sailed - but we perhaps have to think more about learner needs. There is perhaps too much uniformity in teaching and less tailoring to the children's language abilities and needs,' says Tsimpli.

建议是先用儿童能自在理解的语言学习；英语仍可作为一门学科，而不必承担教授所有学科的媒介。that ship has sailed 表示完全撤回英语已不是现实方向。作者批评的是教学过于统一、对能力和需求调整不足，重点在怎样教而非排斥某种语言。

原文片段 · 4

While the preliminary results show there is no difference in general intelligence among boys and girls from slum areas versus those from urban poor backgrounds, an unanticipated finding has been that children from slum backgrounds do not seem to lag behind children from other urban poor backgrounds - and in some cases outperform them (e.g. in numeracy and literacy tasks). According to the researchers, this unexpected finding may be down to the life experiences of children growing up in slums. They are likely to mature faster and come into closer contact with the numeracy skills essential for day-to-day survival.

初步结果中，贫民区儿童在一般智力上并不落后，某些识字与算数活动还表现更好。研究者推测日常生存经验让他们较早接触实用计算，但 may be down to 保留了原因的不确定性。比较对象是其他城市贫困背景儿童，不能直接推成贫困儿童总体优于富裕儿童。

词语与搭配

little room for independent learning

自主学习的空间很少

room 比喻机会和自由度，不是教室面积；与教师占主导的课堂情境相连。

the medium of instruction

教学使用的语言媒介

区分用英语教其他学科与把英语本身作为一门课程，这两者的理解负担不同。

tailoring to the children's language abilities and needs

根据儿童语言能力与需求作调整

tailoring 比喻量体裁衣，强调教学匹配具体学习者，而不是统一提高或降低难度。

essential for day-to-day survival

日常生存所必需的

essential for 后接用途或需要；这里修饰孩子在日常生活中接触的数算技能。

句子精读

Although the findings are at a preliminary stage, Tsimpli and her team have found that the medium of instruction used in schools, especially English, may hold back those children who have little familiarity with, or exposure to, the language before starting school and outside of school life.

虽然研究仍处于初步阶段，Tsimpli 及其团队发现，学校使用的授课语言，尤其英语，可能妨碍那些入学前及校外对该语言不熟悉、接触也较少的儿童的学习进展。

Although 先限定发现的成熟程度，may 再限定影响的确定性。who 从句说明是哪一类儿童；familiarity with 与 exposure to 分别表示熟悉和接触，二者共同指向 the language。不能删掉人群与场景限制。

They are likely to mature faster and come into closer contact with the numeracy skills essential for day-to-day survival.

他们可能更早成熟，也更密切地接触日常生存所必需的数算技能。

They 指在贫民区长大的儿童。are likely to 同时作用于 mature 和 come 两个并列动作，表示研究者的可能解释。essential for day-to-day survival 后置修饰 skills，说明这些技能与生活需要的关系。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

little room for independent learning

自主学习机会不足

用来描述过度由教师控制的课堂，需要说明儿童缺少哪些探索或表达机会。

用于写作：与小学正式教学和课堂游戏的平衡直接吻合，可具体表达过度正式教学的局限。

essential for day-to-day survival

日常生活维持所必需的

只在确实涉及生活压力时使用；可以讨论压力带来的某些实际经验，但不要据此美化贫困。

用于写作：家庭财富题比较成长资源与成年准备；原文提供了生活经验可能培养某些能力的思路，同时例句避免把局部观察扩大为贫困更好的结论。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
The Globemakers · 从生日礼物到制作难题未作答摘要填空 / 观点判断 YNNG · 4 段 · 368 词 · 10 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 90 页

开篇原第1–4段连续裁切，保留A–J完整词表。NG34/35已核对整篇，原文并未给柏拉图所受批评或最早地球仪的准确性评价。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1In 2008, Peter Bellerby, who lived in London, wanted to give his father a model globe for his eightieth birthday. What seemed simple enough to start with triggered an almost obsessive, decade-long journey, marked by a series of obstacles that would have deterred anyone less determined. It ended with his establishing the world's only bespoke globemaking company.

原文片段 · 2The first surprise in The Globemakers, Bellerby's account of this impulsive enterprise, is that obtaining such a globe was not simply a matter of a quick online order and a repressed sigh at the shipping costs. After all, contrary to stubbornly held popular views of our ancestors' geographical ignorance, we have known that the world is spherical since at least the 6th century BCE. 原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1This series of abortive experiments taught Bellerby a lot about the challenges of making globes, which he communicates here to the reader. Finding just the right way to prise the globes from the mould - a high-end air compressor finally did the trick - and locating the right paper and inks with which to make the gores (the sections of flat sheet mapping that are pasted onto the spherical globe) without the ink seeping out to create a mushy, unreadable mess took months and an alarming chunk out of his bank balance. Bellerby's frustration at the painstaking process of attaching the gores to the globe surface - after having found a glue with precisely the right adhesive qualities - is palpable. Right at the end of the process, he learnt that the paper had stretched slightly and so the final one overlapped the first by a centimetre (which may not seem a great deal, but when that represents 2 per cent of the Earth's diameter, it's equivalent to obliterating the Himalayas or wiping out Chile).

原文片段 · 2Bellerby's account of the technical challenges of globe production is interspersed with a series of interludes on great globemakers of the past and cartographic history in general. Purists might wish for more map-making details, but Bellerby clearly found a kindred spirit in Martin Behaim. He was the Nuremberg entrepreneur who in 1492 created the Erdapfel, the world's oldest surviving globe, beautifully finished by a workshop of painters and other craftsmen, only to find that the explorer Christopher Columbus had stumbled upon the Americas the very same year, rendering his masterpiece instantly out of date. Something of Bellerby's unflinching ambition is reflected in the even more heroic efforts of the Italian cartographer Vincenzo Coronelli, who, in the seventeenth century, created two globes for Louis XIV of France. It took him twenty years to complete the monstrous pair, whose vast bulk - each with a diameter of around four metres - can still be admired in the National Library of France in Paris.

原文片段 · 3Although a celebration of the revival of an ancient craft, Bellerby's book is also a lament for the fading away of centuries-old traditions. When he embarked on his globemaking odyssey, he struggled to find artisans with the skills to make the right moulds for the globes or foundries that could shape the meridians (the metal frames which girdle globes) in just the right way. Although he finally located the right craftsmen, some simply dropping in, serendipitously, to his workshop (by now in more suitable premises than his back room), many of these have now retired or passed away.

原文片段 · 4Bellerby's father finally did receive his eightieth birthday present, albeit two years late. Bellerby went on to found a company which now turns out over six hundred globes a year for customers who can have their own tiny village marked or more unusual requests fulfilled. His book, beautifully illustrated with photographs of the various stages of his venture and a few illustrations of historic globes and maps, is hardly a blueprint for commercial success. But it is more than enough to stir up admiration for the craftsmanship of the great mapmakers of the past and the obsessive determination of a modern successor who revived their almost moribund art.

Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

阅读 · 人物匹配 Why we need silence

Match each statement with the correct person, A–D. You may use any letter more than once.

B The World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

C The good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

D Researchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains. 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'

Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience. 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says. 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'

G Eric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress. 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says. Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits. And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think. First, complete silence isn't necessary. In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room. Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits. 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says. 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week. Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'

It is unpleasant and upsetting for people to be placed in a silent environment against their will.

阅读 · 选择题 The World of Sugar

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.
